title: Realization preserves the mixed coefficient restriction square
statement: Fix a prime $l$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_l$, an embedding $\iota:E\to L$, any scheme $X$, and integers $n\le m$. Let $q_E,q_L$ be the actual finite coefficient quotient maps of [def-coef-finite-dualizing-data], and let $i_m,i_n$ be the lifted cross-field quotient maps of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-models]. Given $h_q:q_Li_m=i_nq_E$, set $\eta=c_{q_E,i_n}(h_q)c_{i_m,q_L}(\mathrm{refl})^{-1}$, where $c$ is the ordinary derived restriction compositor. Let $F_{E,r},F_{L,r}$ be the finite comparison-site realizations, $d_{E,h},d_{L,h}$ their quotient restriction comparisons, $b_r$ their cross-field restriction comparisons, and $\eta^\mathrm{int}$ the intrinsic restriction square [def-sf-scalar-reduction-exchange]. For every $K$ in the ordinary small-etale derived category with coefficients $L_n$, one has $F_{E,m}(\eta_K);b_m^{-1}(R_{q_L}K);R_{i_m}^\mathrm{int}(d_{L,h}^{-1}(K))=d_{E,h}^{-1}(R_{i_n}K);R_{q_E}^\mathrm{int}(b_n^{-1}(K));\eta^\mathrm{int}_{F_{L,n}K}$. There is no exceptional functor, dualizing object or scalar-extension mate.

proof.text: On ordinary sheaves, paste the two intrinsic restriction comparisons along each coefficient factorization. Each is normalized as identity on scalar sections. Their pasted section maps are therefore equal; the scalar square hq identifies their coefficient actions. Use the uniqueness clauses in the ordinary intrinsic restriction constructions, including scalarQuotient_restrict for tower restriction.

Localize this ordinary sheaf square. Exact functor composition comparisons are the derivedRestrictScalarsCompIso used in eta. The ordinary-to-proetale comparison restriction maps preserve coefficient composition by the normalized origin comparison coherence.

Whisker the localized intrinsic square with the comparison-site square. Expand the finite realization restriction definitions, use associator naturality and cancel adjacent inverse comparison factors. The two boundaries are exactly the displayed equation; scalarRestrictionSquare uses the same normalized intrinsic compositors.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteRealization_restriction_square {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m)
    (hq : (finiteDualizingQuotient l L h).comp
        (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1} (integralScalarQuotientMap l E L ι m)) =
      (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1} (integralScalarQuotientMap l E L ι n)).comp
        (finiteDualizingQuotient l E h))
    (K : Etale.DerivedCategoryModule (finiteDualizingCoeff l L n) X) :
    (finiteDualizingRealization l E X m).map
        (((Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalarsCompIso X.smallEtaleTopology hq).hom ≫
          (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalarsCompIso X.smallEtaleTopology
            (rfl : (finiteDualizingQuotient l L h).comp
                (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1} (integralScalarQuotientMap l E L ι m)) =
              (finiteDualizingQuotient l L h).comp
                (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1}
                  (integralScalarQuotientMap l E L ι m)))).inv).app K) ≫
      (finiteRealizationRestriction l E L ι X m).inv.app
        ((Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology
          (finiteDualizingQuotient l L h)).obj K) ≫
      (pbcDerivedRestrict (integralScalarQuotientSheafMap l E L ι X m)).map
        ((finiteDualizingRealizationRestriction l L X h).inv.app K) =
    (finiteDualizingRealizationRestriction l E X h).inv.app
        ((Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology
          (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1} (integralScalarQuotientMap l E L ι n))).obj K) ≫
      (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map
        ((finiteRealizationRestriction l E L ι X n).inv.app K) ≫
      (scalarRestrictionSquare l E L ι X h).hom.app
        ((finiteDualizingRealization l L X n).obj K)
